audits.title: Implementing clinical protocols in oncology: quality gaps and the learning curve phenomenon.
audits.standard: Internally developed clinical protocol quality indicators

cycle1.result: Retrospective audit of clinical practice; figures not reported.

audits.intervention: Internally developed clinical protocol applied prospectively with specific tools to increase conformance.

cycle2.result: All indicators improved, many significantly; further improvement in the second part of the prospective study.

audits.other_findings: Advanced age associated (not significantly) with sub-optimal care; learning curve effect seen.
audits.citation: Kedikoglou S, Syrigos K, Skalkidis Y, Ploiarchopoulou F, Dessypris N, Petridou E. Implementing clinical protocols in oncology: quality gaps and the learning curve phenomenon. Eur J Public Health. 2005;15(4):368-371. doi:10.1093/eurpub/cki013. PMID: 16014665.

audits.title: External audit of clinical practice and medical decision making in a new Asian oncology center: results and implications for both developing and developed nations.
audits.standard: Previously reported audit instrument for clinical documentation/quality assurance and decision making
audits.setting: Oncology department in a developing Asian nation (external audit by The Cancer Institute, Singapore)

cycle1.result: Documentation/QA adequate 74.4%, decision making 88.3%, overall 80.2%; 52.0% received suboptimal management.

audits.other_findings: Palliative intent associated with better performance; auditor gave feedback on systematic errors.
audits.citation: Shakespeare TP, Back MF, Lu JJ, Lee KM, Mukherjee RK. External audit of clinical practice and medical decision making in a new Asian oncology center: results and implications for both developing and developed nations. Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys. 2006;64(3):941-947. doi:10.1016/j.ijrobp.2005.08.027. PMID: 16297568.

audits.title: Development and implementation of a medical oncology quality improvement tool for a regional community oncology network: the Fox Chase Cancer Center Partners initiative.
audits.standard: NCCN-derived quality indicators; 20 charts per practice
audits.setting: Fox Chase Cancer Center Partners community oncology network (25 hospitals)

cycle1.result: Stage II/III breast cancer: mean compliance per parameter 88%; 15 of 16 practices achieved mean compliance above 80%.

audits.intervention: Education and documentation tools provided to physicians and nurses
audits.other_findings: Yearly audits over 7 years covered gastric, colorectal and breast cancer.
audits.citation: O'Grady MA, Gitelson E, Swaby RF, Goldstein LJ, Sein E, Keeley P, et al.. Development and implementation of a medical oncology quality improvement tool for a regional community oncology network: the Fox Chase Cancer Center Partners initiative. J Natl Compr Canc Netw. 2007;5(9):875-882. doi:10.6004/jnccn.2007.0078. PMID: 17977500.

audits.title: An audit of the activities of the paediatric oncology unit in Edinburgh, 1982-1991.
audits.standard: Treatment according to national or international protocols, compared with national averages
audits.setting: Paediatric oncology unit, Royal Hospital for Sick Children, Edinburgh

cycle1.result: 92% of patients treated according to national or international protocols in the last five years; 158/240 (66%) children with cancer in clinical remission.

audits.other_findings: A further 69 children with cancer from south east Scotland were treated at other centres.
audits.citation: Saha V, Eden T, Stiller CA, Brown RJ, Mackinlay G. An audit of the activities of the paediatric oncology unit in Edinburgh, 1982-1991. Scott Med J. 1993;38(3):74-76. doi:10.1177/003693309303800305. PMID: 8356428.

audits.title: An audit of the use of agreed treatment protocols at a major centre for cancer treatment.
audits.setting: Department of Clinical Oncology, Charing Cross Hospital, London (major cancer centre)

cycle1.result: Complete adherence to protocol in 84/100; of 16 deviations, 3 unavoidable, 5 minor, and 8 serious departures.

audits.other_findings: Minor deviations were mostly small changes in radiotherapy dose for particular clinical situations.
audits.citation: Glaser MG, Leslie MD, Levison R. An audit of the use of agreed treatment protocols at a major centre for cancer treatment. Clin Oncol (R Coll Radiol). 1995;7(5):304-307. doi:10.1016/s0936-6555(05)80538-2. PMID: 8580056.
